q: A transplant recipient on tacrolimus asks about St John's Wort for low mood. The principal risk is:

o.A: Reduced tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein induction, risking graft rejection
o.C: No interaction, as tacrolimus is renally cleared

q: High-dose garlic supplements taken with saquinavir or other protease inhibitors are a concern because garlic:

o.A: Induces intestinal CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, reducing drug exposure
o.C: Chelates the drug in the stomach

q: Cranberry juice concentrate has been reported to do which of the following in patients on warfarin?

o.A: Raise INR, with case reports of bleeding
o.C: Have no effect on INR in any report

q: Echinacea is considered inappropriate alongside immunosuppressants such as ciclosporin because it:

o.A: Stimulates immune activity that opposes immunosuppression
o.D: Reduces ciclosporin absorption by binding bile acids

q: Fenugreek taken with warfarin and sulfonylureas raises concern because it may:

o.A: Add to anticoagulation and lower blood glucose
o.B: Raise blood glucose and reduce INR

q: Cassia cinnamon taken in large amounts long term is a concern because of:

o.A: Coumarin content and hepatotoxicity risk

q: Yohimbe should be avoided in patients taking MAO inhibitors because it can cause:

o.A: Hypertensive crisis

q: Bitter orange (Citrus aurantium) in weight-loss products is a concern because synephrine:

o.A: Has sympathomimetic cardiovascular effects

q: Passionflower taken with benzodiazepines or sedating antihistamines is a concern because of:

o.A: Additive CNS depression

q: Green tea taken with an iron supplement reduces iron absorption mainly because of:

o.A: Tannins and polyphenols forming insoluble complexes

q: Calcium supplements taken at the same time as ciprofloxacin cause:

o.A: Chelation and reduced antibiotic absorption

q: Zinc supplementation over months at high dose can cause:

o.A: Copper deficiency, with anaemia and neuropathy

q: Niacin at gram doses combined with a statin raises concern for:

o.A: Myopathy and hepatotoxicity

q: Simvastatin taken with grapefruit juice is a concern because grapefruit:

o.A: Inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, raising simvastatin exposure and myopathy risk

q: Dandelion leaf, a mild diuretic, is a particular concern in a patient taking:

o.A: Lithium, because reduced renal clearance can raise lithium levels

q: Uva ursi (bearberry) should not be used long term or in pregnancy because it contains:

o.A: Hydroquinone derivatives with hepatotoxic and irritant potential

q: Aristolochia species are banned as medicines in many countries because aristolochic acid causes:

o.A: Progressive nephropathy and urothelial cancer

q: Which herb is associated with hepatotoxicity and was withdrawn from several markets in the 1990s?

o.A: Germander (Teucrium chamaedrys)

q: Chaparral (Larrea tridentata) is associated with which adverse effect?

o.A: Hepatotoxicity

q: Senna used continuously for many years can cause:

o.A: Melanosis coli and laxative dependence with electrolyte disturbance

q: Pennyroyal (Mentha pulegium) oil is dangerous chiefly because it:

o.A: Is hepatotoxic and has been used as an abortifacient with fatal outcomes

q: Blue cohosh taken in late pregnancy has been associated with:

o.A: Neonatal stroke and heart failure

q: Star anise products have been adulterated with Japanese star anise, which is a concern because it contains:

o.A: Anisatin, a neurotoxin causing seizures, particularly in infants

q: Sassafras was removed from use as a food additive because it contains:

o.A: Safrole, an hepatocarcinogen

q: Dong quai combined with anticoagulants raises concern chiefly because of:

o.A: Coumarin derivatives adding to bleeding risk

q: Raw ginkgo leaf, as opposed to standardised extract, is a concern because of:

o.A: Ginkgolic acids, which are allergenic and cytotoxic

q: Lobelia (Indian tobacco) in high doses causes:

o.A: Vomiting and respiratory depression

q: Coltsfoot (Tussilago farfara) is restricted in some jurisdictions because it contains:

o.A: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids

q: High-dose vitamin D with a thiazide diuretic raises the risk of:

o.A: Hypercalcaemia

q: Long-term proton pump inhibitor use is associated with which nutrient deficiency?

o.A: Hypomagnesaemia

q: Levodopa given without carbidopa is less effective if the patient also takes high-dose:

o.A: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine)

q: Calcium supplements reduce the absorption of which osteoporosis drug if taken together?

o.A: Bisphosphonates such as alendronate

q: High-dose vitamin C taken with an iron supplement:

o.A: Increases non-haem iron absorption

q: Folic acid given with methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis is used to:

o.A: Reduce methotrexate toxicity without abolishing efficacy

q: Zinc supplements reduce the absorption of which antibiotic class?

o.A: Tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones

q: Free T4 is 12 pmol/L on a laboratory reference interval of 10-22 pmol/L. How should this be interpreted?

o.A: Within the reference interval, in the lower part of the range
o.D: Cannot be interpreted without a conversion to ng/dL

q: A serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D of 38 nmol/L is best classified using common Australian thresholds as:

o.A: Mildly deficient or insufficient, warranting correction
o.C: Deficient enough to cause rickets in all cases

q: Using common laboratory thresholds, a serum vitamin B12 of 120 pmol/L is:

o.A: Below the reference interval, consistent with deficiency

q: An HbA1c of 44 mmol/mol (6.2%) in a non-pregnant adult corresponds to:

o.A: Prediabetes range under common guidelines

q: A fasting plasma glucose of 7.4 mmol/L on two occasions is:

o.A: In the diabetes range on repeat testing

q: Transferrin saturation of 55% in a man should prompt investigation for:

o.A: Iron overload, including hereditary haemochromatosis

q: A homocysteine of 18 umol/L is best interpreted as:

o.A: Raised, prompting assessment of B12, folate and B6 status

q: Serum magnesium of 0.62 mmol/L against a reference interval of 0.70-1.10 mmol/L is:

o.A: Low, consistent with hypomagnesaemia

q: An early-morning serum cortisol of 120 nmol/L is:

o.A: Below the typical morning reference interval, suggesting adrenal insufficiency needs exclusion

q: Which combination most suggests iron deficiency rather than anaemia of chronic disease?

o.A: Low ferritin, low transferrin saturation, high TIBC
o.B: High ferritin, low transferrin saturation, low TIBC

q: An eGFR of 42 mL/min/1.73m2 corresponds to which CKD stage?

o.A: Stage 3b

q: A raised ALT with a normal ALP and normal bilirubin most suggests:

o.A: Hepatocellular injury

q: An isolated raised ALP with normal GGT most suggests:

o.A: A bone source rather than a liver source

q: Total cholesterol 6.2 mmol/L with LDL 4.1 mmol/L in a patient with established cardiovascular disease is:

o.A: Above a desirable LDL target for secondary prevention, warranting review
o.D: Indicative of familial hypercholesterolaemia by definition

q: Which finding is most consistent with a functional vitamin B12 deficiency when serum B12 is borderline?

o.A: Raised methylmalonic acid

q: Which presentation most clearly requires urgent medical referral rather than supplement management?

o.A: Unexplained weight loss with night sweats

q: A patient with fatigue is found to have a thyroid nodule with hoarseness. The priority is:

o.A: Urgent referral for assessment of possible malignancy

q: New focal neurological symptoms in a patient being managed for 'adrenal fatigue' require:

o.A: Urgent medical assessment

q: Iron deficiency anaemia in a 62-year-old man requires:

o.A: Investigation of the gastrointestinal tract for bleeding, not just iron replacement

q: Which symptom in a patient with reflux being managed with herbs mandates investigation?

o.A: Dysphagia

q: A patient on a very low-calorie diet presents with palpitations and syncope. The appropriate action is:

o.A: Urgent medical assessment

q: Suspected serotonin syndrome after adding a supplement to an SSRI is characterised by:

o.A: Altered mental state, autonomic instability and neuromuscular hyperactivity

q: Which laboratory result in a patient taking a herbal weight-loss product should trigger immediate cessation and assessment?

o.A: ALT three times the upper limit of normal
